doc.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Writing poetry and lyrics, mostly for his wife Hilma
summary: Carter has written little poetry and song words, mostly for his wife, but no prose.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: So obviously you were a prolific reader even early on in life, and still are, obviously. Did you ever try and write anything? I know you’ve written many, many lyrics. Did you ever try any creative writing or even poetry or anything along those lines?
Well, a little poetry and probably some song stuff without music and written mostly to my wife, Hilma.
What about any sort of prose? Did you ever try your hand at . . .
No, I never did. No, I wrote a letter here and there, but that’s about . . . [laughter]
I’ve seen some of your letters, and I think that some of them are publishable as is.
[laughs] Did you say publishable or punishable?
